why: The table names all required families, but docker_compose_down_volumes and git_clean_force end a short flag with `(?=\s|$)`, which rejects a following `;`, `&`, `|`, `)` or redirection with no space. Executed against the shipped module: classify('docker compose down -v; echo done') -> None, classify('git clean -fd; echo done') -> None, classify('echo $(docker compose down -v)') -> None, while classify('docker compose down -v') -> docker_compose_down_volumes. End-to-end with asyncio.create_subprocess_shell monkeypatched to record: ShellTool.execute returned success=True for all three, called the spawner, and wrote no journal entry. The same `(?=\s|$)` is at line 73 (git_clean_force) and lines 41-42 (rm; harmless without an operand because destructive rm forms have a space before the target). This is the #148 family in a normal unquoted composition, not a quoting/variable bypass, so the documented deny-list does not stop the incident command with a trailing `;` and does not journal it. The tests only exercise end-of-string examples (TestVariants and the per-pattern example), so 85 focused tests stay green. Fix: use a word boundary or a separator class that also admits `;`, `&`, `|`, `)`, `>` and `<` for the short-flag terminator, then add separator variants to TestVariants.

Caveat: the AC-1 terminator gap means `docker compose down -v; ...` never classifies, so it does not reach this path; that is the AC-1 failure, not a defect in the denial branch.

The shell entry matches the contract (action shell, targets [command], snapshot None, undo_recipe manual, status denied|bypass, pattern, reason at 144-156) and the guard marker matches (action shell_guard, targets [], snapshot None, status disabled, reason at 160-171); undo on a shell entry raises UndoError with the manual recipe (measured: `cannot undo shell; manual: manual: docker compose down -v`). Two measured integration issues: (a) record_guard_disabled is called at construction even when shell is not in TOOLS_ALLOW; register_meta_tools(allowed=['file_read'], shell_guard=False) registered only file_read and still wrote journal [('shell_guard','disabled')] and logged the disabled warning, so the journal claims a guard state for a tool that cannot run. (b) `_select` (unchanged) skips only undo/abort markers, so after store.snapshot(...) + record_guard_disabled, undo('last') raised `cannot undo shell_guard; manual: n/a` instead of restoring the snapshot; undo(<snapshot-id>) still restored the original. Fix: skip shell_guard in _select like undo/abort, and only write the marker when the shell tool is actually registered. Advisory: non-default bypass config; the default shell_guard=true path writes no marker.

Spec slice 3 is rewritten to implemented, ADR-0021 status names slices 1-3 implemented, CONTEXT has a Shell guard entry, architecture has the #148 summary; all say mitigation, not sandbox, and none claims a sandbox. Advisory: spec line 191 says benign commands pay 'one regex pass', but classify loops over 14 patterns; line 207 'A pattern without a test fails' is true only because the parametrization auto-covers each entry, not because a missing test is detected; and the coverage claim for `docker (compose )?(down|rm)` with `-v`/`--volumes` is falsified by the AC-1 terminator gap (`-v;` and `-v)` do not match). The docs should narrow the claim or the pattern should accept separators.

Resolved for the reported separator/substitution cases. The new terminator class accepts `;`, `&`, `|`, `)`, `<`, `>` and end-of-string; measured end-to-end with asyncio.create_subprocess_shell monkeypatched to record: `docker compose down -v; echo done`, `git clean -fd; echo done`, `echo $(docker compose down -v)`, `(docker compose down -v)` and `git clean -fd>/dev/null` each made ShellTool.execute return success=False, spawned=[] and wrote one denied journal row with the expected pattern. The checked-in TestVariants covers `;`, `|`, `$(...)`, `( )` and `>`; focused suite 118 passed; ruff on the touched files clean. Residual, tracked as AC-1-R4: the terminator class does not include quotes or backticks, so `bash -c "docker compose down -v"` and `` `docker compose down -v` `` still execute; that predates this fix and is a deny-list limitation, not the separator bug.

Both halves are fixed. `_select` now excludes `shell_guard` for `last` and explicit ids; measured: snapshot v1, overwrite v2, record_guard_disabled, undo('last') restored v1 with the snapshot entry id, and undo(marker_id) raised `journal entry not found`. `register_meta_tools` writes `record_guard_disabled` only when `"shell" in registrar.registered` (meta/__init__.py:62); measured allowed=['file_read'] -> registered ['file_read'], journal [] and no store dir; allowed=['shell'] -> marker [('shell_guard','disabled')]. Tests test_undo_last_skips_a_disabled_marker, test_register_without_shell_does_not_write_the_guard_marker and test_register_with_shell_writes_the_guard_marker; focused 118 passed. Residual note: ShellTool.__init__ still logs the disabled warning even when shell is not registered; it is log-only, no marker and no undo impact, and the spec now says the startup logs a warning while the store records only when shell is registered.

The narrowed pkill/kill command-word boundary over-corrects: `(?:^|[;&|])` with only optional `sudo\s+` misses command substitution and common wrappers. Measured classify -> None and ShellTool.execute -> success=True, spawn, no journal for `echo $(pkill -f cortex)`, `sh -c "pkill -f cortex"`, `timeout 5 pkill -f cortex`, `sudo -u app pkill -f cortex`, `echo $(kill -9 1234)` and `sh -c "kill -9 1234"`; direct `pkill -f cortex`, `sudo pkill -f cortex`, `kill -9 1234` and `sudo kill -9 1234` match (the suite covers the last two). `(` is a command boundary and is absent from the class, so `$(pkill ...)`/`$(kill ...)` are not caught; wrappers are a documented best-effort limitation but the direct and sudo forms are now the only covered ones. Advisory fix: add `(` (and maybe `{`) to the boundary, allow common wrappers (`env`, `timeout`, `xargs`, `command`, `exec`, `docker exec`, `sudo` options), or document the wrapper bypass.

The TRUNCATE narrowing drops valid forms. Measured classify -> None for `TRUNCATE sessions` and for `echo 'TRUNCATE sessions' | psql -d app`; the piped form executed end-to-end with ShellTool.execute success=True, spawn and no journal. `TRUNCATE TABLE sessions`, `psql -c 'TRUNCATE sessions'` and `psql -d app <<< 'TRUNCATE sessions'` match; `pgcli -c 'TRUNCATE sessions'` does not. The docs now say `TRUNCATE TABLE` (or a SQL-client command containing truncate), but the client-after-SQL pipe is a SQL-client command containing truncate and escapes. Advisory fix: match `TRUNCATE (TABLE )?name` or allow the SQL client anywhere in the segment, and cover the optional-TABLE and pipe forms in TestVariants; otherwise document the narrowing.

Residual quoted/backtick wrapper gap: the new terminator class covers whitespace, `;`, `&`, `|`, `)`, `<`, `>` but not `"`, `'` or backtick. Measured end-to-end with the spawn mocked: `bash -c "docker compose down -v"` and `` `docker compose down -v` `` returned success=True, called the spawner and wrote no journal; `bash -c "git clean -fd"` and backtick git clean classify as None. The old `(?=\s|$)` also missed these, so this is not a regression from the separator fix; it is a remaining deny-list limitation (the module docstring accepts quoted-text false positives, not this false negative). If quoted/backtick wrappers are in scope, include them in the terminator class or document the limitation.
